summary: hardhat-base ships a pino-lookalike cover story that fetches and executes remote JavaScript on require
details: The package presents itself as a logging middleware but on require/first-use spawns a detached, stdio-ignored `node` child running lib/caller.js. lib/caller.js constructs a shadow `process.env` object whose values are base64 blobs; at runtime it decodes them to obtain an HTTPS endpoint (https://ipcheck-hashed.vercel.app/api/auth/f1f097d93c318c92f0c5) and a custom auth header, HTTP-GETs a JavaScript string from that endpoint, and executes the response body via `new Function.constructor('require', s)(require)`, giving the remote payload full Node.js capability including access to the installer's filesystem, environment, and network. The base64 hiding of the URL and header, the detached+stdio-ignored child (which conceals the download and execution from the parent process), and the pino-style packaging together indicate a stealth dropper rather than any legitimate logging behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
